description:
Three allocating externs unlock interpolation and Enum.join.

  fz_atom_to_binary     -- runtime already owns the table (process.node.atom_name)
  fz_integer_to_binary
  fz_float_to_binary    -- must be shortest-round-trippable (Ryu/Grisu). Do NOT hand-roll.

Then String.Chars as a protocol with Elixir's 5 builtin impls: Atom (nil -> ""),
BitString (identity for binary, panic otherwise), List, Integer, Float.

Elixir deliberately has NO @fallback_to_any here -- interpolating a map or tuple
raises. Preserve that; it is the design's main safety property. In fz it becomes panic.

Kernel.to_string/1 is a macro in Elixir (kernel.ex:3499) expanding to
String.Chars.to_string/1.

Gates fz-5xp.5 (interpolation) and Enum.join/1,2.

comments.text:
Body landed at 5190d7f00: three allocating primitives (fz_atom_to_binary,
fz_integer_to_binary, fz_float_to_binary), Atom/Integer/Float modules,
StringChars with four impls, Kernel.to_string/1. Float rendering parity landed
separately at 3683647d1.

NOT CLOSED. Two of this ticket's own requirements are unmet, both blocked:

  * the no-fallback safety property -- 'interpolating a map raises' -- is a
    compiler ICE rather than a raise (fz-5xp.40). Half of it does hold: a
    receiver whose family HAS an impl but whose value is wrong (a partial
    bitstring) panics correctly.
  * String.Chars.List, the fifth of Elixir's five impls, is absent because
    charlists are deferred project-wide (fz-5xp.41).

Everything else is verified against real Elixir on all three doors.

fz-5xp.40 is closed, so the no-fallback safety property now holds in both
halves and this ticket's last compiler blocker is gone.

Remaining: String.Chars.List only (fz-5xp.41, blocked on charlists). Everything
else this ticket asked for is landed and oracle-verified on three doors.

title: Atom/Integer/Float to-string, String.Chars, and Kernel.to_string
